records.Description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG), Ship Design & Systems Engineering Division (CG SEA-E4), Human Systems Integration (HSI) Division (WMR-3), Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) and Navy Type Navy Owned (NTNO) Combat Systems Management Division (CG-SEA-E3) share a mission to provide engineering services to support the complete life cycle management of surface assets from concept development through disposal.  USCIS National Records Center (NRC) has a requirement for a contractor to provide support services required under this contract include administrative and technical functions in support of records management for the USCIS Records Operations Support Services (ROSS). The successful contractor is to provide records management and maintenance services for the NRC and NRC Extension Site 1 (ES-1), Lee’s Summit, MO, and its sub-office, the File Storage Facility (FSF or HBG), Harrisonburg, VA.   The objective of the contract is to provide comprehensive records management services in a manner that ensures efficient, effective, and accountable records responsibility and excellent customer service.  The primary functions of this contract include but are not limited to:
 • Provide efficient and effective records management and maintenance functions in support of the USCIS Records Program.
 • Provide outstanding customer service.
 • Ensure compliance with all federal mandated directives.
 • Maintain proper personnel security clearance levels.
 • Ensure proper security of all files, to include empty A-File jackets.
 • Report all personnel actions timely.
 • Ensure proper handling of security-sensitive materials, including PII and chain-of-custody requirements.

 USCIS has a requirement for Information Assurance Security Services (IASS). As USCIS integrates artificial intelligence (AI) / machine learning (ML) and other emerging technologies into our operations, it is imperative to elevate our cyber vigilance. This means ensuring systems are not only resilient to adversarial attacks but also uphold ethical standards that reflect organizational values and societal expectations. The Information Security Division (ISD) seeks a next generation of ISSOs to lead the charge. The IASS resources will continue to perform the day-to-day implementation and validation of IT Security requirements, including ensuring the protection of our systems, data, and environment from malicious users, and to support continuous monitoring activities. These specialized ISSOs are critical to maintaining the security of our systems, assets, and data to avoid or minimize the impact of events.

USCIS has a requirement for Cyber Security Support Services (C3S) II that will utilize GSA HACS 8(a). The C3S-Operations contractor will have a primary responsibility to provide the ability to identify, protect, detect, respond, and recover from cybersecurity threats and incidents. records.Title: USCG Polar Security Cutter Human Performance Support and Training Development
records.Description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) requires a Human Performance Support and Training (HPS&T) system for its Polar Security Cutter (PSC), which will enable crewmembers to employ PSC and PSC systems to execute assigned missions. Required HPS&T services include but are not limited to completion of all analysis, design, development, implementation, evaluation, and maintenance actions necessary to create a complete initial HPS&T system for the PSC program. PSC is essential to America’s Polar region capability. The PSC will conduct extended deployments from homeports and bases in the United States, thus training is an essential part of ensuring that mission critical functions are maintained. Approximately 136 crewmembers, in addition to 20 shore support personnel, will need to be trained to operate and maintain PCSs as expediently and efficiently as possible. Work expected to be performed at contractor's facility, shipbuilder facility in Pascagoula, MS, and other locations, as required.

records.Title: OPC Engine Support Contract
records.Description:
The U.S. Coast Guard Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC), Medium Endurance Cutter Product Line (MECPL), anticipates a requirement for life-cycle support of the FM-MAN 16V 28/33D STC Main Propulsion Diesel Engines (MPDEs) installed onboard the Offshore Patrol Cutter (OPC) fleet.
 The anticipated requirement includes the provision of:
 	1. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)-authorized spare parts, tools, and kits, including preservation, packaging, packing, marking, and delivery;
 	2. Overhaul services for repairable components, including receipt, inspection, repair, testing, preservation, packaging, packing, marking, and delivery;
 	3. OEM-certified technical representatives to provide remote and on-site support for scheduled maintenance and emergent repairs; and
 	4. Operational and maintenance training for cutter crews and shoreside support personnel.
 The FM-MAN 16V 28/33D STC engine is a proprietary system designed by MAN Energy Solutions and supported within the United States by Fairbanks Morse Defense under an exclusive licensing agreement.
 The support services are essential to ensure operational readiness, lifecycle sustainment, and safe, certified performance of the OPC propulsion systems. Performance is anticipated at various USCG locations, including Los Angeles, CA; Newport, RI; ports in Alaska; and additional East and West Coast ports as new OPCs are commissioned.

records.NAICS: 541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
records.Title: Agile Development Services II (ADS2)
records.Description:
Provide skilled information technology labor services to the Coast Guard CG-C5I-Engineering and C5I Service Center Business Operations Division for Agile application development, database maintenance, and custom decision-making tool implementation to improve and modernize technology service delivery to operational Coast Guard units.
 
 Business Governance and Continuous Process Improvement
 - Assess strategic landscapes/events impacting Coast Guard C5I service delivery to define, establish, and update long-term strategic objectives.
 - Conduct research and analysis for strategic growth planning and execution guidance.
 - Engage organizational stakeholders to plan, support and facilitate meetings, determine solutions to stakeholder problems and develop Courses of Action (COA) options to achieve organization goals. 
 - Provide guidance and execution support in defining and measuring effectiveness of governance efforts and assets, and in continually improving governance effectiveness over time.
 - Develop and support Continual Process Improvement (CPI) initiatives by tracking progress, measuring success, and providing training products to support these efforts (for example: Lean Six Sigma White Belt, Yellow Belt, and Green Belt training).
 - Support and provide guidance adopting maturity models, including conducting organizational analyses to research, develop, and execute action plans detailing steps and progress adopting maturity models and steps organizational components should take to mature capabilities in alignment with maturity models.

records.Description: This procurement covers the design, manufacture and installation of one (1) boiler Deaerating Feed Tank (DFT) and all of its associated supporting equipment for installation on USCGC HEALY (WAGB 20) located in Seattle, Washington. The purpose of the DFT is to condition ship's boiler feedwater before it enters the ship's two boilers. This procurement DOES include the installation of the DFT, all hardware and components. Material to be provided but not limited to: One (1) deaerating feed tank package that should be complete with DFT, feedwater piping, vent, gate valves, pumps, gauges, level controls, relief valves, feedwater piping supply, bypass, and overflow piping between the condensate and the DFT, feedwater supply and return piping from the DFT to the boilers. The system should also contain a PLC to control and monitor the boilers, burners and deaerating feed tank. Feedwater treatment system must be NSTM 220V2 compliant. Design must be supported by calculations, diagrams, arrangement drawings and technical publications. Drawings and technical publications are required to be approved before production. Vendor shall supply Provisioning Technical Data (PTD), Attachment 1, with their proposal response that includes certified technical manuals and drawings describing the deaerating feed tank package, control system, and motor controller to provide the United States Coast Guard (USCG) with sufficient information to produce Cutter specific installation drawings. The Vendor shall supply Engineering Data for Provisioning (EDFP), Attachment 2, on the system and components concurrent with the delivery of the equipment to allow the USCG to produce maintenance procedure cards (MPCs) and other logistical support documentation. Engineering data shall also include the PLC code (where applicable) for operation of the system. The Vendor shall provide on-site technical support for training, system testing, commissioning, and certification. The Vendor shall provide maintenance parts lists and a recommended onboard repair parts (OBRP) list for all components.

records.Title: USCGC HEALY Steering Control System
records.Description:
The Coast Guard is planning to replace the steering control system on CGC HEALY located in Seattle, Washington.  The existing steering control system is configured such that rudder angle is controlled from the following helm locations: Main bridge station, (4) secondary conning stations and the steering gear room steering console.  The control system is a combination of electrical and hydraulic equipment with analog backup methods as a redundant fail-safe solution.  All system components and sub-systems (e.g. Rudder Servo Amplifier, Rudder Repeat Back, Rudder Angle Transmitter, and Steering Failure Alarm Panel) shall be replaced with a commercial of the shelf (COTS) in-kind or upgraded technical solution to prevent loss of capabilities. 
 The replacement system must interface with existing auxiliary and navigation systems as defined in the Statement of Work, Coast Guard technical manuals, electrical schematics and drawings.  No proprietary information of the incumbent steering control system will be provided except for the interfacing systems such as electro-hydraulic steering gear and navigation system communications protocols.
 Technical solutions for replacement steering control system must meet the design and safety requirements of 46 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Subparts 58, 111, and 113; the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS); and the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS). 
 The Vendor shall supply Provisioning Technical Data (PTD) that includes certified technical manuals and drawings describing the steering system control system to the United States Coast Guard (USCG) with sufficient information to produce installation drawings.  The Vendor shall also supply Engineering Data for Provisioning (EDFP) on the system and components concurrent with the delivery of the equipment to allow the USCG to produce maintenance procedure cards (MPCs) and other logistical support documentation. Engineering data shall also include the PLC code (where applicable) for operation of the system.  The Vendor shall provide on-site technical support for training, system testing, commissioning, and certification.  The Vendor shall provide maintenance parts lists and a recommended onboard repair parts (OBRP) list for all components.

records.Description:

Required repair services include inspection, component repair, and final testing of components issued from the Aviation Logistics Center to the Contractor and LRU purchase options. records.Title: Information Systems Division Professional Services
records.Description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG), Aviation Logistics Center (ALC) provides logistical support for the aviation fleet and other selected Government agencies. This support includes depot maintenance, engineering, supply, procurement, information services, and acquisition project execution. The ALC, Information Systems Division (ISD) has a need to provide applications development, web development, database engineering, database administration, system engineering, business analysis, system security, procurement, helpdesk support, account management, account auditing, configuration management, quality assurance, project management, asset management, and network support. The ALC ISD is the information technology (IT) department; the primary mission is to provide IT professional services for IT values for ALC on enterprise systems for Aviation Logistics Information Management Systems (ALMIS) and Coast Guard Logistics Information Management System (CG-LIMS) also with ALC’s organic systems, Aviation Logistics Center – Logistics Support System (ALC-LSS). Within the ISD's mission is the task to drive ALC's information technology decisions through the configuration control board, configuration management, system engineering lifecycle, process planning, data analysis and compliance within quality, safety and environmental international standards. The USCG does not have sufficient Government civilian and military personnel to complete required tasks in a timely manner, therefore the USCG will rely on contractor augmentation to fully succeed in this effort. The USCG anticipates competing this requirement as a Service-Disabled, Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside through the General Services Administration (GSA) VETS 2 Governmentwide Acquisition Contract (GWAC).

records.Title: NATIONWIDE AUTOMATIC IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM/VERY HIGH FREQUENCY/DIGITAL SELECTIVE CALLING SUPPORT SERVICES IN ALASKA (NAIS AK)
records.Description:
The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) needs to obtain comprehensive Automatic Identification System (AIS) services, VHF-FM maritime voice communications, and DSC (data) communications for designated regions and ports of Alaska, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
 
 This contract covers four primary functions:
 
 1.	AIS Data and Maintenance Services: The contractor shall provide, manage, and maintain a network of terrestrial AIS sites to ensure the continuous reception of vessel data. This data will be delivered to the USCG to support maritime domain awareness.
 
 2.	AIS Transmission Services: The contractor shall provide the capability for the USCG to transmit messages from shore-based stations to AIS-equipped vessels. These transmissions will support navigational safety, security notifications, environmental alerts, and the broadcast of synthetic and virtual Aids to Navigation (AtoN).  The AIS data and transmission capabilities will be used by the USCG and shared with other Government agencies to support missions including maritime safety, security, environmental protection, and search and rescue.
 
 3.	VHF-FM Maritime Voice Communications: The contractor shall provide, manage, and maintain VHF-FM capabilities to ensure the continuous reception and transmission of VHF communications (VHF CH16) between shore-based stations and vessels in Alaskan waterways beyond the existing Rescue-21 Alaska coverage areas. 
 
 4.	DSC (data) communications: The contractor shall provide, manage, and maintain DSC capabilities (CH 70) to ensure continuous reception of DSC data in Alaskan waterways beyond the existing Rescue-21 Alaska coverage areas.

records.NAICS: 561422 - Telemarketing Bureaus and Other Contact Centers
records.Title: OC3
records.Description:
The purpose of this requirement is to establish multi-award Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPA) for Contact Center support of the GSA MAS NAICS 561422). During periods of high disaster activity, there is a need to respond to incoming calls and perform data entry for individuals and businesses in direct support of disaster activity. The government requires the contractor be prepared to handle up to 175,000 production hours per week. The contractor will have the capability to increase, at FEMA’s discretion, the weekly production hours up to a maximum of 210,000 production hours. FEMA staffing requests may be communicated utilizing Full Time Equivalent (FTE: 1 FTE = 8 Hours/Day x 5 Days/Week = 40 Production Hours per Week). A production hour includes time spent taking calls, in a ready state to take calls, after call work, document validation, 30-minute pre-shift, or directly involved in coaching or training. The government will not pay for call agents unavailable to accept calls due to any lawful permitted breaks exceeding 15-minutes, lunch, or other unproductive time. The Contractor shall provide a fully managed contact center and staff; all costs associated with a scalable contact center shall be included in the agent hour rate. The agent hour/minute billable rate shall be fully burdened; the rate shall include overtime and overhead costs.
 
 PSC Code R702 (Support-Management: Data Collection)

records.NAICS: 541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
records.Title: Performance Benchmarking Tool
records.Description:
The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) seeks a comprehensive software application to optimize mission success by holistically measuring individual traits and performance. The system must enable real-time tracking, analysis, and reporting of student performance and progress to enhance the selection, training, and development of Special Missions Training Center (SMTC) students. Its purpose is to reduce attrition, increase operational capability, and provide evidence-based performance decisions. The database system must generate configurable analytical reports and rollups based on end-user input, capture human attributes related to training objectives, and retrieve historical data to inform assessment or training criteria changes.
 The software application must be compatible with USCG-approved mobile devices and the Non-classified Internet Protocol Router (NIPR) network, allowing instructors to access forms, evaluations, and training materials efficiently. It must include features such as an Automatic Feedback Tool (AFT) to provide tailored feedback based on student performance, a Package Builder for organizing student files, and compatibility with CG Cloud infrastructure for data storage and handling. The system must comply with Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and USCG security standards, Defense Information Assurance Certification Accreditation, and Section 508 accessibility requirements.
 The Contractor shall provide licensing for approximately 750 students and 150 instructors/staff, maintain and update the software, address bugs, and ensure compatibility with technological advancements. Software updates must support curriculum changes, enhance security, and maintain accreditation. The contract must provide scalability for additional licenses, modules, or convenings as operational needs evolve, with flexibility to meet surge training demands within the contract's period of performance.

records.Description:
This requirement is for the acquisition of services to repair components of the APS-143C(V)3 radar needed to support the Maritime Patrol Aircraft Radar (MPA Radar) which is an airborne pulse compression surveillance and imaging radar. It provides the airborne platform with the means to search for and detect surface targets while performing over water surveillance. 
 
 The USCG APS-143C(V)3 radar system consists of three major components: the Receiver/Transmitter (R/T), Part Numbers 737-4000-001 and 737-4000-002, the Signal Data Processor (S/P), Part Number 737-3000-003, 737-3000-004, and the Antenna Pedestal (A/P), Part Number 737-5000-002. 
 
 The OEM for the APS-143C(V)3 radar system is Telephonics Corporation.

records.Title: MH-60T Digital Video Recorder (DVR) System
records.Contract Vehicle: IDIQ TO/DO (Non Strategic Sourcing Vehicle Multiple Award Contract)
records.Description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) Aviation Logistics Center (ALC), Engineering Services Division (ESD), is soliciting proposals from qualified vendors for a new Digital Video Recorder (DVR) system to replace the current obsolete system utilized on the MH-60T rotary-wing aircraft platforms. The existing recording capabilities on board the USCG rotary wing platforms have reached obsolescence and are no longer supportable. This procurement also supports the USCG's transition to High Definition (HD) sensors and the initial integration of this technology into its rotary-wing fleet. This initiative aims to maintain mission effectiveness by ensuring imagery can be recorded and transferred for review and data extraction. The digital video recorder shall store and support the recall of data for event recreation and legal prosecution.

records.Title: Enterprise Gateway and Integration Services (EGIS) III
records.Description:
USCIS has a requirement for Enterprise Gateway and Integration Services (EGIS) III. Historically, EGIS has served as the enterprise integration backbone connecting USCIS internal systems with Department of Homeland Security (DHS), interagency, and external partners. While this core mission remains critical, EGIS will also expand this role supporting national security, immigration system integrity and advanced adjudication operations with key mission including: National security vetting and evolving immigration policies; screening immigration benefit applicants; protecting immigration benefits and work authorization integrity; advanced data integration, analytics, AI-enabled anomaly detection, and decision support; agility, rapid delivery, operational excellence, transparency, and reduced duplication; fraud detection, risk scoring, and investigative data workflows.

records.Title: Asset Tracking Maintenance and Services
records.Description:
The purpose of this requirement is to procure Contractor Support for Asset Tracking Maintenance and Services in support of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Logistics Systems Division's Logistics Supply Chain Management System (LSCMS). The Asset Tracking Maintenance and Services include data infrastructure, network feeds, Global Positioning System (GPS) transponder message pool, hardware upkeep, GPS transponder source-of-supply, facilitation of in-transit visibility, training and supporting personnel. This requirement is needed to support the FEMA Logistics mission with operational and support capabilities for managing the entire disaster supply chain, including FEMA-owned assets and resources, as well as those provided by partners in other federal agencies (OFAs), non-governmental organizations (NGOs), state/local/tribal governments, and the private sector.
 
 The Asset Tracking Maintenance and Services Contractor shall manage the Global Positioning System (GPS) transponder inventory, servicing and activation of GPS transponders, which are identified by Electronic Serial Numbers (ESN) and recorded by the Warehouse Management (WM) application within the Logistics Supply Chain Management System (LSCMS). As transponders are distributed and affixed to FEMA trailers or FEMA assets, the LSCMS application can have in-transit visibility of the movement of the commodity or the asset during a disaster. This in-transit visibility is relayed by GPS feeds via satellite communications. The Contractor shall staff the operational support technicians (OST) located at the FEMA distribution centers. The Contractor is responsible for keeping GPS transponders tested, inventoried, and kitted into surge kits at multiple Distribution Centers for deployment readiness to staging areas at a moment’s notice. The Contractor supports readiness planning, training, and exercise support to enable FEMA staff to perform device management functions during disaster events. The Contractor executes recovery procedures to minimize lost or stolen GPS transponders during disaster operations, provides input on after-action surge lessons learned, and provides recommendations to ensure a continuous improvement cycle for the LSCMS Program.
 
 The estimated Period of Performance is 11/7/2026 through 11/6/2027, with four (4) option years.

 The U.S. Citizenship & Immigration Services (USCIS) has a requirement for Security Operation Analytics Rigor (SOAR), consisting of teams to provide development, security, operations (DevSecOps), data processing and analytic services to support USCIS, Information Technology (IT) development delivery services. These services primarily provide identification of Fraud, National Security and Public Safety concerns. The teams focus will be on performing development, security, and operational support activities. The team will also perform, enhancements and refinements of algorithms as well as standardizing large-scale, complex, internal and external applications. 
 
 All applications in the portfolio employ a baseline set of DevSecOps development postures along with USCIS required development gates, safeguards and requirements. They can be categorized into several overarching categories: Case Management, Investigation, Data Storage / Operations, Screening and Vetting, Immigration Operations, Immigration Law Enforcement, and Intelligence Operations.

records.Title: Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) Program Management Office (PMO) Support
records.Description:
This requirement is for contractor support to provide three Agile-driven teams to deliver program management, risk management, and knowledge management services for the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP)systems and programs. The Contractor will support performance measurement, process improvement, data analytics, requirements management, and business case development for SEVP operations. Responsibilities include developing and maintaining risk management plans for the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) Programs Section and System Management Unit. The Contractor support team will coordinate risk reviews, provide independent risk assessments, and manage risk inventories and mitigation strategies. Additionally, the Contractor team will support the operational management of program documentation and knowledge libraries within the SEVP Assessment Management System (SEVPAMS), ensuring proper version control and metadata management. Strategic planning and administrative support will be provided to facilitate efficient operations, compliance with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) privacy and information assurance policies, and continuous improvement of SEVP systems and processes. The scope excludes software development and focuses on management, administration, and support functions.
 
 Based on the market research results, this requirement will be solicited as a 100% Small Business Set Aside against OASIS+ SB – Management and Advisory Domain, Category 10108, NAICS 541990 - All Other Professional, Scientific and Technical Services; Size Standard: $19.5 Million, in accordance with the procedures RFO FAR 16.507-5.

records.Title: U. S. COAST GUARD POLAR SECURITY CUTTER (PSC) PROJECT RESIDENT OFFICE PASCAGOULA (PROPGLA) TECHNICAL SUPPORT SERVICES
records.Description:
The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is acquiring highly capable Polar Security Cutters (PSC). The USCG Project Resident Office Pascagoula (PROPGLA) is responsible to the USCG Surface Acquisition Directorate (CG-SEA-A6) for oversight and management of the production and delivery contracts for the PSCs that are being constructed at Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding (BMS) located in Pascagoula, Mississippi (MS). PROPGLA is co-located with BMS.  The USCG PSC Program is currently building the first of three PSC Heavy Icebreakers.  The PSC build cycle is approximately five years elapsed time from start of construction to delivery.
 The purpose of this acquisition is to obtain Contractor Acquisition, Logistics, Configuration Management, and Technical Support Services to support the United States Coast Guard (USCG) Project Resident Office Pascagoula (PROPGLA).
 These support services require on-site personnel at PROPGLA facilities, and on-demand surge support to augment PROPGLA capability as dictated by ship construction issues and PROPGLA resource availability.
 Specialties of work to be performed include: Quality Assurance (QA), C5I Systems Technical Subject Matter Expertise (SME), Engineering Technical Program Management, QA Process and Deficiency Records Management, Acquisition and Life Cycle Logistics, Configuration Management (CM), Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Property Management, Project Management, Test Plan Management, Test Verification and Validation, Data Management, and Government Furnished Material (GFM) Management.

records.Title: FY26-RECON ENV Support Rpl Water System (Kodiak) PN 32248420
records.Description:
The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) requires an innovative, long-term solution to manage contaminated environmental media at Base Kodiak, Alaska. This program aims to drastically reduce the generation of soil spoils from construction activities and to develop a permanent facility capable of treating contaminated soil.
 
 This Scope of Work (SOW) outlines a multi-phased design-build project. The contractor shall provide a complete solution encompassing initial feasibility studies for soil reduction, pilot-scale testing of advanced treatment technologies, and the final design and installation of a contaminated media segregation pad and permanent soil management facility.  The objective is to develop an integrated soil management system with capabilities to perform onsite soil treatment. An assessment of available treatment technologies shall be conducted with an onsite pilot test determining the effectiveness of treating listed contaminants. There will likely be more than one treatment technology needed to treat contaminants of concern (COCs).

records.Title: Continuous Synopsis Record
records.Description:
This contract is essential to ensure the U.S. Coast Guard fulfills international maritime security obligations under the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) by maintaining accurate Continuous Synopsis Records (CSR) for the U.S. flag fleet.  Under the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), the United States is legally obligated to maintain an up-to-date Continuous Synopsis Record (CSR) for all applicable vessels. Executing this contract ensures the U.S. Coast Guard remains compliant with these binding international maritime safety and security standards. 
 
 A failure to maintain these records degrades our ability to monitor maritime threats and compromises international security protocols. The administrative bandwidth required to process, update, and manage these records across the fleet is substantial.  Dedicated contractor support is required to execute this essential administrative function. Without this contract, CG-CVC will lack the necessary administrative capacity to process CSRs in a timely manner. This would result in international non-compliance, potential delays or detentions of U.S. flagged vessels in foreign ports, and a degraded posture in global maritime security tracking.

records.Title: Replace Boat Bay Roof at Sector Northern Great Lakes, Sault Ste Marie, MI - PSN 12165041
records.Description:
Replace Boat Bay Roof at Sector Northern Great Lakes, Sault Ste Marie, MI - PSN 12165041
 
 1. WORK INCLUDED: Major items of work shall include the following: 
 1.1 Remove the existing metal fascia and wood blocking at roof edges. 
 1.2 Remove existing single ply EPDM roof system including roof membrane, roof flashings, 
 roof insulation and roof edge to expose the existing concrete roof deck. The existing flat portion 
 of the roof is constructed with tapered insulation sloping to roof drains. 
 1.3 All existing roof top equipment is scheduled to remain. All existing roof penetrations are 
 scheduled to remain. 
 1.4 The contractor shall provide temporary heating or cooling to allow for the maintenance of 
 68 degrees F heat minimum with existing or temporary heating equipment or 78 degrees F 
 maximum with existing or temporary cooling equipment. 
 1.5 Install new Polyvinyl-Chloride (PVC) roof system including new tapered roof insulation, 
 multiple ply roof membrane with ½” gypsum cover board, associated roof flashings including 
 various base and pipe penetration configurations. Existing roof drains shall be in sump pans. 
 1.6 Provide and install new curbs at roof top HVAC units to accommodate new roofing 
 thickness. Secure split-system air conditioners to new roof. Disconnect, remove, store, and 
 protect the existing exhaust fans during re-roofing operations, then re-install to the original 
 condition on a new curb. No electrical, mechanical, or controls work outside of disconnection 
 and reconnection is called for. 
 1.7 Install new wood parapet wall at roof edge to accommodate new roofing thickness and 
 install new metal fascia. Install scuppers at Admin/Barracks roof and Galley roof. 
 1.8 Install new overflow drains (4 locations) and 5” cast iron piping under the roof structure 
 down to outlet at 36” above grade. 
 1.9 Work associated with these items are described in the following specification sections 
 and/or are shown on the contract drawings. Incidental work items not listed above and necessary 
 for completing the project shall be included.

records.Description:
***09/02/2026: Changes include, update to requirement description, update to Fiscal Year, update to estimated solicitation release date, update to estimated period of performance start date, update to estimated period of performance end date, update to anticipated award date.***
 
 The USCIS Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate, Immigrant Investor Program Office, has a requirement to procure access to the Sayari graph analyst platform to support fraud detection, national security, and public safety screening and investigative activities. The platform will assist FDNS personnel in identifying, analyzing, and documenting connections among individuals, businesses, corporate entities, trade activity, and related ownership structures.
 
 Sayari graph analyst aggregates corporate, trade, and risk-relevant data from more than 250 jurisdictions and provides network analysis capabilities to help identify relationships, ownership interests, affiliations, and other links that may not be readily apparent through standard research methods. These capabilities support FDNS efforts to detect fraud indicators, assess potential public safety concerns, and identify national security-related risks associated with USCIS adjudicative and investigative workloads.

records.Description:
CBP has an ongoing requirement to interdict contraband including, but not limited to weapons, explosives, illegal drugs, and currency, through the examination of various conveyances. As part of its layered enforcement strategy, CBP officers utilize Non-Intrusive Inspection (NII) systems like Low-Energy Portals (LEP) for inspecting smaller vehicles such as privately owned vehicles (POVs), including cars, sport utility vehicles, pickup trucks, motorcycles, commercial vans, dual-rear wheeled trucks, and towed trailers, as well as Multi-Energy Portals (MEP) for inspecting larger, occupied commercial vehicles, including buses, recreational vehicles, and truck tractors with laden semitrailers and trailers. records.Title: Thales FY27
records.Description: USCIS has a requirement to obtain the software license renewal for Thales Device HSM (Hardware Security Module) as a Service which is a key component of the overall device certificate automation project. An HSM is a specialized physical device designed to securely store and manage digital keys, cryptographic operations, and sensitive information. They provide a high level of protection for cryptographic processes and serve as a secure foundation for various security applications. Additionally, they offer a range of features including key generation, storage and protection, cryptographic operations (such as encryption and decryption), secure key exchange, and digital signatures. By employing tamper-resistant hardware and robust security mechanisms, HSMs help safeguard sensitive data and cryptographic keys from unauthorized access and tampering attempts. They also support compliance with regulatory standards and provide a trusted platform for building secure systems.

records.Title: Gigamon FY27
records.Description: USCIS is looking to renew the Gigamon software license which is a platform that meets the following requirements. Compliant Deployment Model: The network TAPs must be on-premises physical devices as they are required to be placed in-line of the physical network cables. The network TAPs must support private cloud deployment to be placed in-line with USCIS cloud deployed instances. Supportability: The network TAPs must offer active TAPs to amplify and mirror network traffic. The network TAPs must be able to support copper and fiber optic network traffic. The network TAPs vendor must offer a passive TAP to limit interference with network traffic. The network TAP must support up to 100GB bandwidth of network traffic. Filtering: The network TAP must support port mirroring and aggregation. The network TAP must be able to filter on source and destination IP addresses, port numbers, protocol, VLAN, MAC address, and content. The network TAP should be able to filter on encrypted SSL/TLS traffic. Management: The network TAP must be able to be managed from remote locations and support centralized management. Native OCSF Support: The TAP system must support sending data compliant with the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF).

records.NAICS: 541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
records.Title: Risk Methodology and Programmatic Support
records.Description: The mission of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)/Grant Programs Directorate (GPD)/Homeland Security Programs Division (HSPD) is to effectively develop and administer FEMA’s preparedness grant programs which aim to help improve the capacity of state, local and tribal entities to prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from natural and manmade hazards, including acts of terrorism. HSPD accomplishes this mission by developing and administering numerous grant programs in close concert with Federal, state, local, tribal, nonprofit, and private stakeholder consultation. HSPD supports the grant process of allocating grant funding to numerous grant programs by developing a comprehensive risk methodology that is used to inform grant allocation decisions. In managing its risk methodology, GPD evaluates threat, vulnerability, and consequence factors to determine the relative risk of states, territories, large urban areas, and tribal nations. GPD is also required to ensure that its efforts support the requirements of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, as amended, as well as DHS and FEMA senior leadership priorities. It is also imperative that GPD works closely with stakeholders internal to GPD, FEMA, and DHS and with stakeholders external to FEMA including state and local first responder communities, as well as private sector partners. DHS program offices that support the grant programs are: the Transportation Security Administration and the United States Coast Guard; DHS components that work with risk data such as the Office of Intelligence and Analysis (I&A), Office of Operations Coordination/Special Events Program, and the National Risk Management Center; Custom and Border Patrol, and other public/private entities that own and/or manage sources of risk data. The activities under this Performance Work Statement are intended to analyze the relative risk of states/territories, and the 100 most populous Metropolitan Statistical Areas in the United States for the purpose of informing allocations under the GPD preparedness grant programs. Risk Methodology and Programmatic Support will provide HSPD with the services necessary to support the development of risk methodologies used to inform grant funding and analytics measuring the preparedness grants for states, territories, urban areas, ports, and transit system. The Contractor will be part of an integrated team, participating with federal employees and other Contractors to support GPD’s strategic and tactical objectives. The Contractor shall provide all necessary support services to meet the tasks and deliverables defined in the following functional project areas: -Support the current Grant Risk Methodologies -Future risk strategies development -Programmatic monitoring and oversight. The Contractor shall provide solutions, options, and recommendations to the Government through a review and approval process. The Government will determine all courses of action for implementation, and the Contractor will assist in the development project implementation plans on a timeline schedule on request.

records.NAICS: 541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
records.Title: Coast Guard Civilian Labor & Employee Relations Branch (PSC-CPM-2) Performance Management Program and Case Management System (CMS) Support
records.Description:
The Office of Civilian Workforce Relations, Civilian Labor and Employee Relations (PSC-CPM-2) provides direct advisory services to operational commands related to civilian accountability. This encompasses conduct and performance-based actions, leave misconduct, medical inability, reasonable accommodations in connection with employee relations matters, union grievances, and settlements. This requirement merges two (2) critical support services:
 
 Performance Management Program Support: The Performance Management Program requires additional professional program management and administrative support to meet new legislative requirements and departmental directives. Current personnel resources are insufficient to sustain daily operations, respond to complex data calls, and conduct mandated quality assurance activities. 
 
 Case Management System (CMS) Modernization: Following a 2019 Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Inspector General (OIG) report and a 2022 Secretary memorandum, the Coast Guard (CG) is required to meticulously track misconduct allegations and outcomes on a quarterly basis. The current CMS (implemented in 2025) must be modernized to accommodate incoming CG employee populations, incorporate additional data fields for complex cases, and generate specific reports for the Department and Office of Personnel Management (OPM). A real-time accountability database is required to promote transparency, consistency, and collaboration across the CG. 
 
 This unified contract will stabilize daily civilian performance workflows and ensure 100% data integrity and compliance with DHS Misconduct Governance Board (MGB) quarterly reporting mandates. Contractor physical hardware is not provided; access will be remote via Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI/Manta).

records.NAICS: 541990 - All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
records.Title: Hermit's Peak Arbitration Support
records.Description: The United States Congress introduced and passed into law H.R. 7721, known as the Hermit's Peak Fire Assistance Act (“Act”). This Act aims to provide compensation to victims affected by the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon Fire, which was caused by a prescribed burn on Federal land in April 2022 resulting in significant devastation, including the burning of 325,340 acres of land and the estimated destruction of 900 homes and structures. To administer the claims resulting from the fire, the Act mandates the establishment of the Hermit’s Peak/Calf Canyon Claims Office (referred to as the “Claims Office”), which is operated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). The Claims Office’s responsibilities include receiving, evaluating, processing, and disbursing actual compensatory damages to the victims of the Hermit’s Peak/Calf Canyon Fire. The Government seeks an Advisory and Assistance Support (A&AS) Contract to provide qualified arbitrators to the Hermit’s Peak/Calf Canyon Claims Office. FEMA estimates up to 1,846 arbitrations hearings to take place during the Period of Performance of this contract, with 35% of cases occurring during the Base Period, 55% occurring in Option Period 1, and 10% occurring in Option Period 2. FEMA estimates a weekly average of up to 10 arbitration hearings.

records.Title: Enterprise Open-Source Investigations Software Solution
records.Description: USCIS seeks an enterprise-grade open-source investigations research tool capable of collecting, analyzing, and visualizing publicly available information (PAI). The tool should enable authorized users to monitor, search, and extract relevant data from multiple publicly and commercially available sources in real time, supporting mission-critical investigations, threat assessments, and situational awareness. Additionally, the solution must reduce the amount of time analysts spend manually reviewing open-source content by automating the collection, analysis, and surfacing of derogatory information. The platform must provide a persistent misattribution environment to enable secure and anonymous research, user-level account maintenance and support, and a user-friendly interface. Finally, the solution should include integrated subject recognition capabilities, automated derogatory information surfacing, and the ability to perform batch querying for efficient processing of multiple subjects.

records.Title: On-Site Compliance Assessment Support Services for ICE 287(g) Public Safety Partnership Division
records.Description:
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) seeks contractor support to conduct approximately 1,000 comprehensive, on-site compliance assessments over the course of one year of Law Enforcement Partner (LEP) agencies participating in the ICE 287(g) program under the Task Force Model (TFM) and Warrant Service Officer (WSO) Model. The contractor will provide qualified compliance assessment personnel or teams to travel to LEP facilities, perform detailed operational and programmatic reviews, collect and analyze data, conduct interviews, and prepare findings and compliance reports for ICE ERO. Contractor personnel will work with the appropriate ICE ERO Field Office to facilitate corrective action plans and submit final reports.
 
 The Contractor shall furnish all personnel, supervision, equipment, and materials necessary to conduct approximately 1,000 on-site compliance assessments per year of LEP agencies under the TFM and WSO models. The Contractor will be responsible for all aspects of the compliance assessment process, including pre-assessment planning, on-site activities, data collection, interviews, post-assessment analysis, and reporting.
 
 Contract services will include but are not limited to pre-assessment planning, coordination with partner agencies, document review, on-site assessments, interviews, credential reviews, operational observances, report preparation, corrective action recommendations, and final report submission.
 
 The total period of performance for this effort is 36 months comprised of one 12-month base period of performance beginning on the date of contract award and one 2-year option period exercisable at the Government’s discretion. 
 
 The Contractor shall ensure adequate contracted staffing to meet the operational requirements of this contract, and provide qualified, experienced personnel.

records.Title: United States Coast Guard (USCG) Response Boat – Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
records.Description:
The Response Boat – Small Third Generation (RB-S III) represents the USCG's recapitalization of the 29-foot Response Boat-Small (RB-S II). The RB-S fleet consists of approximately 400 boats designed for a 15-year service life, with a top speed exceeding 40 knots, and exhibiting exceptional maneuverability. As the USCG’s primary asset for Search and Rescue (SAR), Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS), and Law Enforcement (LE) missions in coastal areas, the RB-S needs to be capable of towing vessels up to 10 tons displacement. The RB-S III will maintain the primary mission requirements of its predecessor, with potential expanded roles in Drug Interdiction (DI) and Migrant Interdiction (MI) operations. The USCG plans to acquire up to 400 boats, with the option for other Government agencies to order up to 100 additional modified variants. In addition to the boats and trailers, the program will include delivery of the following support elements: 
 
 Technical Data: Drawings, 3D models, Bill of Material (BOM), and commercial manuals to support the development of maintenance instructions. 
 Interim Contractor Logistics Support (ICLS):  ICLS (labor and material) to sustain the boats until organic Coast Guard Support has been established. 
 Spares: Initial provisioning spares for the first year of operation and system insurance spares (e.g., fenders, spare engines). 
 
 The USCG plans to award up to four (4) contracts in FY2027, each with a minimum order quantity of one (1) boat, and order one (1) boat from each contract. These boats will be operated to verify the delivered boats align with the previously submitted and evaluated paper proposals. At the conclusion of this process, a single boat builder will be selected to produce the RB-S III fleet.
 
 All information in this forecast is for planning purposes only and is subject to change pending approval of the acquisition strategy and supporting acquisition documents. This forecast does not constitute a solicitation, presolicitation notice, or Government commitment.

records.Title: Card Upgrade and Redesign of Equipment (CURE)
records.Description:
The Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), requires a comprehensive solution for the production and personalization of secure identification cards under the Card Upgrade and Refresh of Equipment (CURE) program. The requirement includes supporting the USCIS Office of Intake and Document Production, Document Management Division, in delivering a redesigned card and card production system for Permanent Resident Cards (PRC) and Employment Authorization Document (EAD) cards at the Corbin, Kentucky and Lee’s Summit, Missouri production facilities.
 
 The requirement includes the design and high-volume manufacturing of a new secure card constructed of 100% polycarbonate with embedded Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) and metallized optically variable devices. The card design must be configurable for multiple immigration benefit types and future document types, allowing for updates to artwork, color schemes, and mastheads. Fulfillment of the requirement includes providing card stock storage and a card personalization solution capable of producing both the new and legacy PRC and EAD cards until legacy stock is depleted.
 
 The requirement includes installation and ongoing maintenance of the card personalization system, development of an operator user interface, integration with existing USCIS information systems, and support for system acceptance and user acceptance testing. The solution must include user training and technical support. The system must support high-volume production, scalable to at least ten million cards per year per site, and provide redundancy to meet continuity of operations requirements.
 
 All solutions and services must comply with Department of Homeland Security Enterprise Architecture policies, technical reference models, and data management standards. Hardware and software maintenance must be provided as well as system upgrades, consumables management, and operational support for both production sites. The system must include automated and manual quality assurance, inventory management, card tracking, and reporting capabilities. Reports must cover inventory, card production, scanning issues, rejected cards, work in progress, and other operational metrics.
 
 The requirement includes delivery of all required documentation, including project management plans, system design documents, training materials, interface control agreements, supply chain risk management plans, and system transition plans. All personnel must meet security and background investigation requirements for access to sensitive but unclassified information and government facilities. Fulfillment of the requirement includes equipment delivery, installation, integration, and testing.

records.Title: LITHIUM-ION BATTERY FIRE TESTING
records.Description: The increasing use of electric micro-mobility devices (EMMD) such as electric bicycles (e-bikes) and electric scooters (e-scooters) by tourists and daily commuters has introduced new risk vectors to maritime transit. Because these transit modes carry passengers and their EMMDs concurrently, commercial passenger ferries represent a unique environment where a lithium-ion battery fire could present severe risk to life safety and vessel survivability. The USCG requires a study on thermal runaway propagation and suppression agent effectiveness on lithium-ion batteries in common shipboard EMMD stowage configurations. The primary objective is to acquire high-fidelity empirical data to characterize lithium-ion battery fire behavior and severity resulting from an e-bike fire on a commercial ferry and evaluate current maritime suppression methods. This data will guide future policy for vessel fire safety and crew training and response.

records.Description:
The Coast Guard is planning to conduct specific sub-system recapitalizations in support of the CGC HEALY Service Life Extension Program (SLEP) from FY2027 to FY 2031. A number of these system recapitalizations require integration and tie-in to the existing Integrated Power Plant (IPP) system. The existing IPP system is comprised of the Central Power Plant (common bus electric propulsion and auxiliary power generation systems) and selected components/systems in the auxiliary machinery plant, which is maintained/managed by a separate services contract. 
 
 This acquisition is a multi-year contract with the scope focusing on the integration of the recapitalized sub-systems into the IPP system. The sub-systems intended to be recapitalized currently include: the Science Sea Water System Pump and Cyclone Separator, Steering Control System Components, Sanitary System Components, Over-the-Side Weight Handling System, Deaerating Feedwater Tanks, and the Bow Thruster. The IPP system is proprietary and the USCG intends to award to a sole source for this acquisition to the Original Equipment Manufacturer. The Vendor shall provide on-site technical support for training, system testing, commissioning, and certification. The Vendor shall provide maintenance parts lists and a recommended onboard repair parts (OBRP) list for all components.

records.Title: USCGC HEALY (WAGB-20) Service Life Extension Program Anchor Handling and Controls Parts Procurement
records.Description: The Coast Guard is planning to procure two new anchor windlasses assemblies and their associated major spare part sub-assemblies to replace the obsolete anchor windlasses on USCGC HEALY located in Seattle, Washington.  The HEALY requires two anchor windlass assemblies, one configured for port and one configured for starboard installation. The assemblies shall include the complete mechanical assembly including the capstan head, gypsy head, gearcase, mechanical/hydraulic brakes, hydraulic motor, brake control stands, centralized greasing system and interconnecting components. This procurement does not include installation of the equipment but does include limited technical support by the Contractor to the United States Coast Guard (USCG) to ensure that the equipment is installed correctly and functions correctly.  The anchor windlasses must meet the design and safety requirements of 46 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Subparts 58, 111, and 113; the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS); and the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS). The Vendor shall supply Provisioning Technical Data (PTD) that includes certified technical manuals and drawings describing the system controls to the United States Coast Guard (USCG) with sufficient information to produce installation drawings. The Vendor shall also supply Engineering Data for Provisioning (EDFP) on the system and components concurrent with the delivery of the equipment to allow the USCG to produce maintenance procedure cards (MPCs) and other logistical support documentation. Engineering data shall also include the PLC code (where applicable) for operation of the system. The Vendor shall conduct a factory acceptance test of the system and shall provide on-site technical support for training, system testing, commissioning, and certification. The Vendor shall provide a maintenance parts lists and a recommended onboard repair parts (OBRP) list for all components.

records.Title: Program Management Support for Financial Systems Modernization
records.Description:
The DHS Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO) established the Financial Systems Modernization (FSM) program to oversee Component FSM efforts. The foundational tenets for the FSM programs are:
 • Increased business process standardization across Components through efforts to define a common set of financial management business processes and then ensuring Component business process re-engineering and modernization efforts reflect the DHS process standard.
 • Implement standard financial data element structures such as the DHS Accounting Classification Structure (ACS) and Common Appropriation Structure (CAS) across Components to standardize reporting and reduce manual reporting processes and inconsistent data.
 • Continue to plan and execute financial system modernization projects by migrating Components to a modernized platform or integrating financial systems with asset and procurement management systems that meet Department-wide requirements and financial system and business process standards. FSM projects should also leverage existing infrastructure, shared services, and technologies such as cloud-based solutions to the extent possible, following guidance and lessons learned from previous attempts to integrate DHS Components' financial management systems.
 • Lastly, after standardization and modernization has occurred, DHS will work toward consolidating financial operations and transaction processing service centers where cost effective.
 •	DHS has established the Enterprise Financial Systems (EFS) office, formerly known as the Joint Program Management Office (JPMO), to lead and manage all aspects of the FSM programs, in partnership with DHS Components. Roles and responsibilities for the EFS are defined in the EFS Charter and other governance documents.
 
 CISA’s Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO) established a Project Management Office (PMO) to manage its FSM initiative at the Component-level. This PMO is comprised of a project manager and systems accountants. It established an FSM Integrated Project Team (IPT) to provide programmatic and functional expertise to manage and support the FSM transition and potential migration. Due to the resource-intensive nature of the Discovery and implementation phases of migration, CISA’s FSM PMO requires programmatic and technical support to assist in the modernization effort.
 
 This requirement provides continued technical, functional, and program management support for CISA’s Financial Systems Modernization (FSM) effort throughout the implementation phase, and preparation for enterprise-wide deployment. Contractor support includes data management and migration support, system integration coordination, and functional expertise necessary to maintain momentum across FSM phases and ensure readiness for transition to a modernized DHS financial management solution. These subject matter experts (SMEs) are critical support roles to ensure financial data integrity, continuity of business processes, and a seamless integration to the unified system approach across the Department.
 
 OBJECTIVE
 The objective of the FSM PMO Support is to support CISA OCFO throughout the lifecycle of the FSM Program, in partnership with EFS, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as its financial services provider, and the DHS system integrator, so that the FSM solution is: configured to meet CISA requirements; CISA Financial Data is prepared so that it is able to be migrated to the future solution; CISA users are apprised of the migration and are trained and ready to accept the system upon go-live.

This requirement is for the manufacture and delivery of steel foamfilled

 ATON buoys to guide mariners in the navigable waters of the United States. The
 type of buoy that is specifically used in the rivers of the Midwest is known as a
 "river buoy." River buoys are continually lost or destroyed on station through
 collisions with passing vessels, extreme weather conditions, or simply through
 wear and tear in the harsh marine environment. These buoys must therefore be
 replaced in large numbers. On average, about three-quarters of all river buoys
 deployed on station are replaced annually. There is a need to establish a
 contract for the manufacture and delivery of river buoys to meet the USCG's
 operational requirements for these aids.

records.Title: Scalable Integrated Navigation System Generation 2 (SINS-2) Follow-on
records.Description:
Background and Purpose:
 The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) requires a follow-on Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract to procure next-generation Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) marine navigation systems. This effort is the successor to the Scalable Integrated Navigation System 2 (SINS-2) program (Contract HSCG44-17-D-170005) and aims to recapitalize and modernize the standardized electronic navigation suites across the USCG's diverse fleet of cutters and boats.
 Scope of Work:
 This contract is for hardware and associated chart subscriptions; installation and maintenance will be handled via separate actions. The contractor shall provide a scalable suite of COTS marine electronics that are interconnected via a NMEA 2000 compliant backbone. The core components include, but are not limited to: Multifunction Displays (MFDs) in various sizes (e.g., 4-6", 7-8", 10-12"), Radome and Open Array radar systems, GPS receivers, depth sounders with multiple transducer options, and heading sensors. The scope also requires the provision of updated electronic navigation charts for all procured systems. All hardware must meet the ruggedization and EMI/RFI standards outlined in IEC 60945.
 Technical and Cybersecurity Requirements:
 The system must be interoperable with existing USCG infrastructure, including the capability to process and display Encrypted Automatic Identification System (EAIS) data as specified in the EAIS Interface Design Description (IDD). All procured hardware, firmware, and software must adhere to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) cybersecurity directives and Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) protocols. The contractor must also have a robust obsolescence management plan, providing form, fit, and function replacements for components with a minimum of 18 months' notice.
 Period of Performance and Scalability:
 The anticipated Period of Performance is a two-year base period with eight one-year option periods, allowing for a total of ten years. The contract must be highly scalable to ensure continuous lifecycle support for the current fleet and to serve as a strategic bridge to future navigation system technologies, mitigating any potential fielding delays.

records.Title: M&R Bldg 205 SSO Locker
records.Description:
The SSO Locker Building (Bldg. 205) serves as the sole ready gear locker/wet room facility at Sector New York. The building is a single story 5291 SF prefabricated modular structure constructed in 2006 on a concrete block foundation with a flat roof and surrounded by a faux brick skirt. The building contains Male and Female locker rooms, heads, wet rooms and storage spaces. The roof has numerous leaks. The fire alarm system no longer functions (due to water intrusion) and the building lacks emergency egress signs and modern lighting. The building (essentially a large locker room/head) is not ventilated (non-code compliant construction) and contains a continuous strong musty odor. The ½” thick exterior brick facade architectural panels are peeling away from the building. The wooden access staircases and doors are rotting. The vinyl flooring has rips and gashes throughout caused by the flexing of the poorly supported under flooring. 
 
 SCOPE:
 Summary: This project will replace the roof and façade, replace the entryways, add ventilation, replace the fire alarm and replace the flooring/sub-floor.

records.Title: Ports and Waterways Safety System (PAWSS) IDIQ Preventative, Corrective and Adaptive Maintenance
records.Description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) C5I develops, builds, fields, trains, and supports advanced electronic command, control, and navigation systems. The USCG uses a modified version of the Lockheed Martin Corporation (LMCO) Maritime Traffic Management (MTM) software as a key component of Ports and Waterways Safety System (PAWSS). Supporting the USCG's Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) mission across the continental US and Alaska, PAWSS provides vessel tracking, correlation and Command & Control (C2) capabilities. The USCG installed PAWSS at nine Vessel Traffic Center (VTC) units with sensors & related equipment at 67 remote site facilities. PAWSS operates on a 24/7 schedule and has a subject availability of 99.75% per VTC unit. The system is a highly tailored product designed to meet USCG requirements. PAWSS is an Information System (IS) that resides on the CG One DHS network. It consists of a base set of software components provided by LMCO as part of their MTM software suite integrated with commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) RADAR and Automatic Identification System (AIS) components, as provided by USCG C5I. Continuation of LMCO sustainment operations, maintenance and engineering development services are required for continued lifecycle management of PAWSS.

records.Title: Tier 5 Background Investigation Support
records.Description:
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Office of the Chief Security Officer (OCSO), requires contractor support to conduct non-personal services related to personnel security processing for federal employees, contractors, and other vetted partners. The contractor shall provide all personnel, materials, and services necessary to execute personnel security actions, including Entry-on-Duty (EOD) processing, fitness determinations, suitability adjudications, and eligibility evaluations for access to National Security Information (NSI).
 This requirement includes full lifecycle support for the procurement and completion of Tier 5 background investigations and the delivery of Reports of Investigation (ROIs) needed to determine security eligibility. Work must adhere to established CISA and DHS personnel security processes, investigative guidelines, and program standards. All information handled under this effort, including any government provided data or contractor collected investigative material is designated For Official Use Only (FOUO) and must be managed in accordance with the Privacy Act of 1974.
 The contractor shall conduct these services nationwide, including U.S. territories, and provide case-based program management and administrative support. records.Title: National Benefits Center (NBC) Records Operation Contract (ROC)
records.Description:
"In support of the processing of applications and petitions for adjudication of immigration benefits, the National Benefits Center (NBC) Records Operations Contract (ROC) provides non-inherently Governmental services that encompass a wide range of pre-processing activities in order to accomplish the mission-essential functions required at the NBC. The primary functions of this contract include, but are not limited to, Correspondence Management (e.g., courier services, file and mail management, and monetary instrument handling); Case Preparation (assembly of various applications or petitions in accordance with USCIS policies and procedures); File Control and Maintenance (e.g., file merging, A-File creation, and case updates); Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) scanning (the scanning of all documents within a file(s) and the upload into the designated FOIA system); and Program Management.  NBC ROC services are provided at the NBC locations in Lee's Summit, MO and Overland Park, KS.  
 
 NBC's mission is to create and support the centralization of the pre-processing required to support the Field Offices under the Field Office Directorate (FOD). NBC ROC supports the following mission critical functions: (1) Mail, File & Data Entry/scan support for over 2.5 million applications annually (2) Support for Freedom of Information Act requests (3) Large-scale file room operations, reducing the need for records support staff and space at field offices (4) Pre-processing activities for over 3 million applications and petitions annually (5) Case preparation and review for approx. 800,000 Adjustment of Status applications (6) Initiation of requests for initial evidence for approx. 300,000 Adjustment of Status applications annually (7) Manual Name Harvesting for security checks, saving officer resources and improving processing times (8) Tracking and monitoring of case work and adjudication-ready cases (9) Management of workflows for over 1 million records adjudicated at the NBC."

records.Title: Permanent Change of Station (PCS) Relocation Software System (PCS-RSS)
records.Description: Acquisition of a software solution to execute Permanent Change of Station (PCS) relocation management system while seamlessly interfacing with Coast Guard Financial and Human Resource management systems, ensuring complete data integrity and fiscal accountability. The objective is to modernize and streamline the entire relocation lifecycle for uniform and civilian members. For this requirement, the vendor must: - Provide a cloud solution that has achieved and maintains a Provisional Authorization (PA) from the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) at Impact Level 4. - The solution must ensure and maintain full compliance with Joint Travel Regulations (JTR), Federal Travel Regulations (FTR) and United States Coast Guard Supplement to the JTR (CGS-JTR) for domestic and overseas moves. The system’s business rules and calculations must automatically reflect all current regulations. - The system must be capable of securely and efficiently facilitating approximately 25,000 PCS relocations annually. Performance must be stable, reliable and provide an intuitive user experience for both transferring members and administrative personnel. - The solution must manage the entire PCS lifecycle within a single, integrated system. This includes automated processing of pre-trip authorizations, amendment, financial obligations, post-trip vouchers, de-obligations, final disbursements, and tax computations. - The solution must establish and maintain a reliable, two-way interface with the USCG’s financial management system. The contractor would be responsible for the complete lifecycle of the provided software solution, ensuring it remains compliant with all applicable federal, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and USCG specific regulations.

records.Title: Operational Test and Evaluation Support Services for USCG Commander, Operational Test and Evaluation Force
records.Description:
This requirement provides comprehensive engineering, technical, and analytical support to Commander, Operational Test and Evaluation Force (OPTEVFOR) in executing its role as an independent Operational Test Agency (OTA) for U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) acquisition programs. The objective is to ensure USCG systems are independently assessed for operational effectiveness, operational suitability, and cyber survivability under realistic, fleet-representative operating conditions prior to full-rate production decisions and fleetwide deployment.
 
 Scope encompasses end-to-end Operational Test and Evaluation (OT&E) lifecycle support across major USCG acquisition domains, including surface cutters, aviation platforms, unmanned systems, Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, and Intelligence (C5I) systems, and enterprise mission software. Support activities span the full acquisition lifecycle, including Early Operational Assessments (EOA), Operational Assessments (OA), Initial Operational Test and Evaluation (IOT&E), and Follow-on Operational Test and Evaluation (FOT&E).
 
 Key technical and analytical support tasks include:
 
 Test Design & Framework Development: Applying Mission-Based Test Design (MBTD) methodologies to develop Integrated Evaluation Frameworks (IEFs) that decompose mission requirements into Critical Operational Issues (COIs), Key Performance Parameters (KPPs), Measures of Effectiveness (MOEs), and Measures of Suitability (MOSs).
 
 Test Planning & Documentation: Authoring rigorous, event-specific Operational Test Plans (OTPs), data collection and management plans, environmental threat matrices, and safety briefs aligned with USCG Major Systems Acquisition Manual (MSAM) guidelines and DHS/DoD acquisition directives.
 
 Operational Test Execution & Data Collection: Providing on-site technical support during underway, flight, and shore-based test events, managing automated and manual data collection instrumentation, executing realistic operational scenarios, and conducting cybersecurity operational test and evaluation (adversarial assessments and vulnerability assessments).
 
 Data Analysis & Independent Evaluation Reporting: Processing complex operational telemetry, qualitative operator feedback, and cyber vulnerability data; applying rigorous statistical and scientific methodologies; and drafting comprehensive Operational Test Agency (OTA) evaluation reports and executive briefings to inform USCG Executive Leadership and the DHS Acquisition Decision Authority (ADA).
 
 Programmatic & WIPT Coordination: Participating in Test and Evaluation Working-level Integrated Product Teams (T&E WIPTs), reviewing draft Test and Evaluation Master Plans (TEMPs), and collaborating with USCG Acquisition Directorates (CG-9), requirements sponsors, and developmental test stakeholders.
 
 Support will primarily be performed at OPTEVFOR headquarters in Norfolk, Virginia, with occasional travel to USCG operational bases, shipyards, flight test facilities, and underway cutter deployments.

records.Title: Illicit Drug Trace Detection
records.Description:
The United States Coast Guard’s (USCG) maritime law enforcement mission includes countering illicit narcotic trafficking. Maritime law enforcement encompasses armed intervention by uniformed Coast Guard personnel, conducted both aboard vessels and at facilities ashore, to detect and suppress violations of applicable law. 
 To support this critical mission, USCG units are authorized to conduct Contraband Detection Activities (CDA) to determine the presence of contraband. CDA involves the use of organic, mechanical, or chemical devices that sample or examine the air or physical surfaces to detect narcotics or explosives. The purpose of this project is to acquire and field advanced Narcotic Trace Detection (NTD) devices to fulfill this operational CDA requirement.

records.Title: Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) Services
records.Description:
Task Area 1: Integrated Logistics Support and Equipment Provisioning
 
 2.0.1 Scope and Compliance. The Contractor shall provide business, inventory, and logistics support services in strict accordance with applicable directives, including the Financial Resource Management Manual-Procedures (FRMM-P), Electronics Manual, DHS Systems Engineering Life Cycle (SELC), and C5ISC Configuration and Change Management Policy. The Contractor must supply qualified personnel, supervision, and operational resources necessary to execute all assigned delivery orders under this contract.
 
 2.0.2 Logistics Systems and Provisioning. The Contractor shall execute data entry, maintenance, and research within electronic supply and logistics databases, including the Fleet Logistics System (FLS), USCG NESSS, and DLA WebFLIS, utilizing both graphical and character-based interfaces. Responsibilities encompass managing parent/child Configuration Item (C/I) data, nomenclature development, Allowance Parts Lists (APLs), new item enrollment, existing C/I reprovisioning, and acquisition-focused market research for part replenishment and repair. Personnel must actively support configuration analyses to remediate supply chain discrepancies and optimize inventory posture.
 
 2.0.3 Documentation and Technical Data Support. The Contractor shall collaborate with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to develop, evaluate, and revise comprehensive SELC and acquisition documentation. Deliverables include System Support Plans (SSPs), Equipment Support Plans (ESPs), Supply Item Change Records (SICRs), Item Entry Proposals (IEPs), Supply Support Requests (SSRs), Integrated Logistics Support Plans (ILSPs), Time Compliant Technical Orders (TCTOs), standardized configuration drawings, desk guides, and weekly accomplishment reports.
 
 2.0.4 Configuration Management Execution. The Contractor shall deliver CM planning, identification, change control, status accounting, and audit support. The Contractor must ensure only approved, validated modifications are incorporated into technical documents and software baselines. Support includes evaluating Engineering Changes (ECs) and providing independent assessments of technical data packages, job aids, and illustrated parts breakdowns.
 
 2.1 Task Area 2: Business Management and Process Development
 
 2.1.1 Business Management Support Services (BMSS). The Contractor shall provide non-inherently governmental BMSS directly supporting C5I command priorities, including DoD Enterprise Service Management Framework (DESMF) adoption, Mission Support Business Model implementation, and organizational change initiatives.
 
 2.1.2 Process Analysis and Change Management. The Contractor shall evaluate current ("as-is") workflows to detect bottlenecks and redundancies, designing optimized ("to-be") processes using industry-standard modeling tools. The Contractor shall facilitate cross-functional stakeholder workshops, execute change management strategies to maximize user adoption, author Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and deliver comprehensive training materials.
 
 2.1.3 Continuous Improvement and Metrics. The Contractor shall establish robust metrics, tracking dashboards, and post-implementation audit protocols to evaluate process effectiveness and sustain a culture of continuous improvement across the organization.
