records.Description:
The Transportation Security Administration System Integration Facility (TSIF) is in Arlington, VA at the Reagan Washington National Airport.  It is a 128,000 sq. ft. two story building equipped with three elevators.  The TSIF building was purchased by TSA from the United States Postal Office in October 2010 and is situated on Metropolitan Washington Airport Authority (MWAA) property. The operations and maintenance (O&M) of the building’s exterior infrastructure (façade, windows, and roof), parking lot paving and striping, ground floor baggage handling equipment, and sidewalk maintenance (excluding snow removal) are managed by the Building Property Manager and are excluded from the scope of this Task Order. 
 
 The Freedom Center is housed in Herndon, VA and consists of 104,014 rentable square feet (103,502 usable square feet per BOMA standards) in a single-story building.  The Freedom Center (FC) was established in response to the direction provided by the National Strategy for Combating Terrorism, as part of the President’s Management Strategy.  Operational since July 2003, the Freedom Center serves as TSA’s 24/7 coordination center for transportation security-related operations, incidents, or crises for TSA within the Department of Homeland Security.  It integrates real-time intelligence and operational information, ensuring unity of command and action in preventing and responding to terrorist-related incidents across all transportation modes (maritime, land, and aviation).
 
 TSA requires complete operations and maintenance services for the above-referenced facilities. The Contractor shall ensure all required project management, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, grounds maintenance, and housekeeping (including janitorial, custodial, equipment and systems testing/inspection, preventive/predictive maintenance, corrective maintenance/repair, 24/7/365 operations, and emergency services) are performed to provide a safe and comfortable environment for building occupants. Preventive maintenance service calls must meet or exceed commercial standards. All tasks must comply with applicable codes, laws, regulations, and policies at all levels. Services must be provided 24/7 for the Freedom Center and 5 days per week for the TSIF facility.
 
 TSA anticipates issuing a contract for these services under the AbilityOne Program.

records.NAICS: 541990 - All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
records.Title: Employee Parking Assistance Program (EPAP) Support
records.Description:
The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) is charged with protecting the nation’s transportation systems to ensure freedom of movement for people and commerce. Recruiting and retaining a highly skilled and trained workforce necessary to staff passenger and baggage screening checkpoints across the nation is critical to agency operations. To support this, the TSA Employee Parking Assistance Program (EPAP) provides a simplified means for TSA to subsidize parking, the cost of which is a recurring concern among the workforce, which reduces administrative burden on TSA. In accordance with the authority vested with the TSA Administrator and applicable fiscal law, some employees are eligible for fully subsidized parking, while others are eligible for partially subsidized parking, and some are not eligible for any parking subsidies.
 
 TSA requires a Contractor to remit parking fees on behalf of the TSA at all required locations for all participating employees. Contractor support is also required to coordinate parking locations for TSA employees along with shuttles to transport employees from parking lots to and from their work location(s). The Contractor must be able to provide the above referenced services at all TSA locations nationwide and in all U.S. Territories, including, but not limited to, over 440 airports and field offices.

records.Title: National Hazardous Materials Management & Disposal Services (VAP)
records.Description:
Prior to passage of the Aviation and Transportation Security Act (ATSA), Pub.L. 107 71, the air carriers were responsible for the screening of commercial air carrier passengers.  They also were responsible for the collection and disposition of all prohibited items, including hazardous materials.  With the passage of ATSA, TSA became responsible for the screening of these passengers.  49 U.S.C. §44901(a).  
 
 As a result, TSA determined that it had the legal responsibility to accept prohibited and hazardous items abandoned by passengers at security checkpoints.  Having accepted the property, TSA is legally liable for the disposition of abandoned or forfeited personal property.  Hazardous materials, if not otherwise donated per 41 CFR 101-42.304, must be disposed of in accordance with Federal and state laws and regulations.  42 U.S.C. §6901 et seq.
 
 In 2003, TSA issued the National Voluntarily Abandoned Property and Hazardous Material Disposal Contract to assist with the management, disposition and disposal of the prohibited and hazardous items abandoned by passengers at security checkpoints.  In April 2005, TSA added lighters to the prohibited item list as directed by Congress in the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004. Liquids, Gels, and Aerosols (LGA) were also added to the prohibited list in August 2006 while lighters were removed from the prohibited list in August 2007.  As a result, the type and amount of hazardous items abandoned by passengers at security checkpoints have changed and increased in quantity since April 2005.
 
 TSA requires a Contractor to provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, vehicles, supervision, and other items and services necessary to perform hazard materials management and disposal for approximately 450 airport locations (and ancillary TSA offices when necessary).  The number of airports and airport locations is subject to change throughout the life of any resultant contract depending on privatization and Federalization decisions, new airports opening, the operation of seasonal airports or reorganizations that affect TSA operations.  Services shall be performed for all airports/collections areas.  The Contractor must meet or exceed all Federal, State, and local regulations.

records.NAICS: 541611 - Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services
records.Title: Federal Financial Systems Support Services
records.Description:
TSA’s current financial system is the Financial System Modernization Solution (FSMS), which is a suite of applications that includes Oracle Federal Financials (OFF), Sunflower Assets (SA) and Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM). FSMS also integrates with TSA feeder systems which automate certain business processes, such as Concur Government Edition (CONCURGOV which is the employee travel management system) and MarkView (for invoice imaging and approval workflow). In addition to these feeder systems, TSA uses the National Finance Center (NFC), a service-based organization to process payroll from the U.S. Treasury Department and distribute payment to TSA employees. To reflect payroll transactions in FSMS, the NFC payroll files are downloaded and processed on a bi-weekly basis to update the FSMS general ledger. These systems integrate with FSMS to ensure that all financial transactions are properly posted to the general ledger. TSA supports the TFDW (an Oracle Data warehouse) utilizing Oracle Business Intelligence Applications (OBIA) /Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition (OBIEE) /Oracle Data Integrator (ODI)/ Oracle Application Express (APEX) that is hosted in the Amazon Web Service (AWS) Cloud by DHS. TSA provides Database Administration (DBA), OBIA/OBIEE development/maintenance/enhancements to a suite of business Dashboards and Reports for 600 users.
 
 TSA requires a Contractor to support the oversight of the financial systems service provider and provide functional and business intelligence (BI) support to the TSA financial systems user community. Effective systems management and associated services will facilitate successful accomplishment of overall financial management objectives.
 
 TSA does not operate or maintain the production systems; nor does TSA perform system development work to modify the financial systems (those are our service provider’s responsibilities). TSA develops BI reports and administers the OBIA/OBIEE/ODI/APEX environments to support the TSA user community. The principal purpose of the solicited service is for the Contractor to provide financial management systems functional and BI support. The solicited services will be performed primarily within the TSA Chief Finance Office (CFO) and require a unique combination of functional and technical expertise in a Federal financial management system environment with a heavy emphasis on the Federal financial, accounting, and financial systems functional expertise. Specifically, TSA requires Contractor support to: 1. Provide overall project and task order management support; 2. Provide overall financial systems implementation support services and operations and maintenance which include, but are not limited to, general IT control activities, financial systems functional support, and travel system support; and 3. Provide Data Warehouse and Oracle BI Support, which include overall Data Warehouse/BI Support Activities, Project Lead and BI Architect Support, DBA Support, BI/OBIA Administration Support, and BI Development Support.

records.Title: Appian Enterprise Plan
records.Contract Vehicle: NASA Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement VI (NASA SEWP VI)
records.Description: The US Coast Guard (USCG) Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, and Intelligence (C5I) Software Yard requires an Appian Enterprise Plan (licenses, environments, maintenance) to provide a secure, scalable, and unified Low-Code Application Platform (LCAP) that supports mission-critical business processes, enhances operational efficiency, and improves data management and collaboration across organizational units. Appian, as an LCAP, enables rapid development and deployment of IT capabilities by abstracting and minimizing, or completely replacing, the need for traditional coding. Its low-code features, including model-driven and graphical programming approaches, allow for the creation of complete applications or capability modules, such as user interfaces, business logic, workflow, and data services, with little to no coding required.

records.Title: DETACHED DUTY RECRUITER CO-WORKING SPACES
records.Description:
In response to the absence of brick-and-mortar offices in detached locations, where U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) recruiters operate, the USCG is initiating a program to contract coworking spaces. These spaces are essential for maintaining professionalism and privacy while conducting interviews and meetings crucial for recruitment efforts. Recruiters in detached locations also have the responsibility of assessing the need for permanent recruitment presence. Providing them with dedicated workspaces supports day-to-day activities and aids in evaluating the necessity for long-term recruitment resources. This initiative underscores the USCG's commitment to effective recruitment by ensuring recruiters have the necessary support to represent the service professionally and engage with prospective candidates effectively.
 
 The contractor shall locate and contract, through evaluations and assessments for up to sixteen (16) locations, facilities that meet the specified criteria. The contractors shall document its selection process and provide justification for chosen locations.

records.Title: Nationwide Regional Facilities and Administrative Services (RFAS)
records.Description:
The TSA Facilities and Administration (F&A) program office serves as the agency's physical and operational backbone by managing its extensive real property portfolio and nationwide facility footprint. F&A is responsible for lease management, strategic space planning, and facility maintenance. Additionally, F&A coordinates critical logistical support, manages personal property assets, establishes occupational safety, health, and environmental standards, and oversees essential administrative services to ensure that frontline officers and administrative staff have functional and fully equipped workspaces to protect the nation's transportation systems.
 
 F&A requires streamlined, flexible, and highly responsive acquisition vehicles to provide a comprehensive suite of facilities-related products and services. TSA anticipates establishing multiple-award, regional Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) for commercial products and services such as structural and finishing trades; mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP); custodial services; heavy equipment and appliances; and logistics and transportation services. BPA Holders would need to be able to service all TSA locations within the identified region: Northeast, Southeast, Central, and Western. This includes CONUS and OCONUS locations.

records.Title: Next Generation Electron Navigation (eNav) Software Solution
records.Description:
The purpose of this project is to acquire a navigation software solution that meets applicable maritime standards and the operational requirements of the United States Coast Guard (USCG). The software must support a range of equipment configurations based on platform-specific mission requirements—from basic navigation capabilities for smaller boats to integrated, multi-user systems for larger cutters.
 
 The navigation software will provide users with accurate and timely information to support the safe navigation and operation of Coast Guard boats and cutters. It will also promote fleet-wide standardization, improving consistency for both system operators and maintainers.
 
 A typical configuration will integrate Global Positioning System (GPS) capabilities compatible with other Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), radar, depth-sensing equipment, and heading sensors. The system will also interface with external Automatic Identification System (AIS) and Digital Selective Calling (DSC) equipment to obtain and display target data.
 
 The navigation system shall support data distribution through the following protocols and standards:
 •	Multicast User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
 •	Unicast UDP
 •	Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP), operating as a client
 •	TCP/IP, operating as a server
 •	National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA) 0183
 •	NMEA 0183-HS (high-speed)
 •	NMEA OneNet
 •	NMEA 2000

A MAST system uses commercial off-the-shelf sensor technologies, including maritime surface search radars, EO/IR cameras, encrypted AIS receivers, a Mission Management System, and payload platforms. The Contractor must provide all system administration duties including upgrades and optimizations to maintain the GCCS-J production system hardware (e.g., servers, workstations, and associated peripherals, etc.) configurations in an operational status. The Common Operational Picture (COP) environment includes distributed data processing, data exchange, collaboration tools, and communications capabilities. The COP also includes information relevant to the tactical and strategic levels of command and control. This includes, but is not limited to, geographic information systems data, assets, activities and elements, planning data, readiness data, intelligence, reconnaissance and surveillance data, imagery, and environmental data. The Contractor must provide system support services to manage the system administration, system availability and reliability of GCCS-J shore production systems (current and future versions) on a 24/7 basis.
